proposal: To encourage dependable generic drug manufacturing, the Mandate recommends that FDA replace pass/fail facility inspection outcomes with a graded system recognizing manufacturers that invest in reliability, add facility codes to drug packaging with a searchable database cross-referencing product and facility codes, that HHS exempt multi-source generic drugs from Medicaid and other federal rebate requirements, and that FDA and NIH promote efficacy trials of new uses of generic drugs (p. 457).

status_summary: FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research has continued a voluntary Quality Management Maturity prototype assessment program, with notices on 2025-04-23 and 2026-02-11 opening second and third years for up to nine volunteer establishments that receive scored reports; the notices do not say scores are published. Executive Order 14293 of 2025-05-05 directed FDA to consider publicly listing noncompliant facilities and to disclose foreign inspection counts by country and manufacturer, which is related to but not the same as facility codes on packaging or a graded inspection system. No step on exempting generics from rebates or on NIH or FDA new-use trials was found.

timeline.event: FDA published a notice opening a second year of the voluntary Quality Management Maturity prototype assessment program (up to nine establishments, scored reports to participants).

Executive Order 14293, Regulatory Relief To Promote Domestic Production of Critical Medicines (published 2025-05-08), directed FDA to improve enforcement of drug establishment data reporting, including considering public display of a list of noncompliant facilities, and to disclose annual foreign inspection counts by country and manufacturer.
FDA published a notice opening a third year of the voluntary Quality Management Maturity program, accepting requests through 2026-04-13.
